module: Sharps (from BBP) · COM: Manufacturing · Frontline worker · Host and expert interview

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Someone who empties the bins on a production line told us this: "It wasn't my needle. I never even saw it go in the bin."

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [warmly] I'm Dana.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: And I'm Ray.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [curious] Ray, you've worked at a few different plants over the years. [playful] What changes for you, walking into a new one?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Everything you can see changes... the machines, the layout, the people. But I still catch myself looking for the same small habits right away, because they tell me more than any sign on the wall.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [realizing] Small habits are where today's subject lives, too: the needles and other sharps people use and throw away at work.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [curious] A guy on the line takes insulin on his break. He's at a table in the break room with the syringe in his hand. Needles always felt like a hospital thing to me, so why is that syringe your business on a plant floor?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Because it's a sharp, and a sharp is any medical needle, or anything else that can cut or puncture skin. Needlesticks are especially common in healthcare. But on plant floors they're a real and growing risk, as more people give themselves shots for diabetes, allergies and other conditions.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: And once he's used it, why does that one needle still worry you?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [concerned] It still holds a little blood. And it's so sharp that chances are high it sticks someone else by accident and exposes them to that blood.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: That's a lot of risk in something so small. Let's turn this to you, listening on your shift... before he takes the cap off, what should he do first?

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Okay, Ray, tell us what he should do first.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [firmly] He plans FIRST, how he'll handle the needle and where it goes after. For him, that means finding the slot on the sharps container on the break-room wall.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: So he's done, and his hands are full with the syringe and his lunch. There's a trash bin right under the table. What do you tell him?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [matter-of-fact] Not that bin. If there's a needle-free option, he uses that in the first place. If the syringe has a safety feature, he turns it on. Then it goes in that container immediately.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Immediately. If he worked in a clinic instead, what would you tell him then?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [thoughtful] In healthcare settings, used needles can't be bent, broken, recapped, removed or separated from the syringe. They go in a sharps container immediately or as soon as possible.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: So what's your short version for him?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: He knows where it's going before he starts, the same as he would before cleaning up broken glass. He uses a needle-free option if there is one, turns the safety feature on, and drops it in that container right away.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [amused] Next coffee run, I'm looking for that box on the wall.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Every bag of trash on a production line ends up in somebody's hands. Jacob empties the bins along the line when each shift ends, and he's here to tell you about one night on that job.

lines.speaker: JACOB
lines.text: [tired] The last bin I empty is by the loading door. Same every night. That night, I lifted the liner out and went to tie it off. Then I saw it. A needle tip, poking through the plastic, right where my hand was going. I let go. I just stood there. [quietly] It wasn't my needle. I never even saw it go in the bin. Walking out, I passed the break room. The sharps container was up on the wall, same as always.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: That close. Tell me what he'd have been facing if it had stuck him.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [concerned] A stick can expose you to bloodborne pathogens, meaning germs carried in blood, like H-I-V, hepatitis B and hepatitis C. Those could lead to severe health complications.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Some people figure a used needle is only a risk to the person who used it. How do you answer that?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [patient] A needle that isn't thrown away properly can hurt someone further down the line, like the person handling the trash, who NEVER touched it. So the way you get rid of a sharp directly affects someone else's risk of getting hurt. [slowly] And it only takes one shortcut, on one busy day, to cause a serious injury... maybe an infection that changes a life.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: I keep seeing that bag by the loading door, and his hand already reaching to tie it.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: A needle can push through the fingertip of a thick work glove.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [thinking out loud] So say a plant has to choose. Thicker gloves for everyone who handles the trash, or more sharps containers, like the kind mounted on a break-room wall. [wry] I'd have bought the gloves. Which would you pick?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: The containers. Gloves are P-P-E, the protective gear you wear, and P-P-E alone works less well against needlesticks than engineering controls. An engineering control is something built into the workplace, like that container on the wall. The best protection is a proper sharps container, because it takes the hazard away before anyone can touch it.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: [skeptical] Then those gloves would just be for show?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: No, they earn their place. Heavy-duty gloves made of nitrile, latex, vinyl or neoprene can protect your hands from cuts and from hazardous substances. I just wouldn't count on them against a needle.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Walk me through what the container actually changes out on a plant floor.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [matter-of-fact] A safety-engineered sharps container closes the sharp inside the moment it drops in. In manufacturing settings, that cuts down on accidental needlesticks, and on bloodborne pathogens passing from one person to another.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: So once the containers are up, do they do the job by themselves?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [thoughtful] No. People lean toward the easiest path, and the containers and the training both have to beat that habit. At more than one plant, I've watched people walk RIGHT past a container to the nearest trash bin.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Picture the spot where you work. How far is it from there to the nearest sharps container?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [warmly] If you can't picture it right away, that's worth a walk on your next break.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: That container on the wall only works if the needle actually ends up inside it.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: So let's stay with one that didn't.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: I've walked past boxes like that on a wall for years without a second look.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [wry] Then it's worth hearing what that box does that a pair of gloves can't.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: A trash bin by the door and a container on the wall. Only one of them was made to hold a needle.

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Picture someone on your line with a syringe in their hand on a break.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Before that cap comes off, could they point to the nearest sharps container? Could you?

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Somebody empties the bins on your line at the end of every shift.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: [thoughtful] Next time you drop something in one, whose hands lift that bag after you?

lines.speaker: DANA
lines.text: Think about the gloves you pull on at the start of a shift.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Now think about the sharps container closest to where you work. Which one would you trust with a used needle?
